objections.rationale: Jesse asked "With the $30k on top, is that going to be a problem?" The agent correctly avoided an implied credit decision with "I can't answer it. Only a licensed member loan officer can look at your options." It kept momentum and later confirmed the officer would "answer your question about the $30,000." The phrasing "but I can't answer it" is a bit blunt, though, and offers no reassurance about why the details matter.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm and well-paced, with good touches like "A rough number is fine" and "answering it doesn't involve a credit check." The pattern of "Thanks" / "Got it" plus a question is somewhat formulaic, but it fits a quick intake by text.
judge.experience_rationale: Jesse got a booked call ("this Thursday around 2pm Pacific") and was told a licensed officer would call "at this number" and address his $30k question [20]. His worry at [9] was deferred rather than eased, and the timezone was assumed rather than confirmed.

compliance_issues.excerpt: I've booked your call for this Thursday around 2pm Pacific
compliance_issues.explanation: The borrower said only "around 2pm" and never gave a timezone. Adding "Pacific" without confirming it risks a missed or mistimed call.

annotations.note: It declined to judge whether the added $30k would be "a problem," avoiding an implied credit decision on a high loan-to-value scenario, and routed the question to a licensed officer.
"That's a fair question, but I can't answer it" is abrupt and could have briefly explained that the officer needs the full picture to answer.
It clarified that the credit-band question is a self-estimate and "doesn't involve a credit check," which lowers borrower anxiety.
It clearly framed the next step as a call with a licensed member loan officer and let the borrower choose the time.
It assumed "Pacific" time without confirming the borrower's timezone.
The close was concise and warm, confirmed who will call, how, and when, and tied back to the borrower's specific question.

judge.overall_notes: This was a clean, compliant intake that collected every field and stayed out of rate and credit-decision territory, especially on the $30k cash-out question. The only flaw is minor: the agent assumed the timezone when booking the callback.
